short: Ports a 2023 ECoG recipe (text-to-speech HuBERT units, CTC) to EMG; phoneme guidance (M02) and covariance input (M06) are standard. Its own text route beats direct synthesis: 51.17% vs 61.02% WER.
position: The paper [@gowda2025emg2speech] ports to surface EMG the ECoG synthesis pipeline it says it adopts [@metzger2023]: HuBERT units from text-to-speech audio, learned with CTC and voiced by a pretrained vocoder. Its own changes, an auxiliary phoneme CTC head with a consistency loss (M02) and a covariance input from the same group's earlier work (M06) [@gowda2025], are standard; auxiliary phoneme losses for EMG voicing date from 2021 [@gaddy2021improved]. The strongest confound is the paper's Table 6: its own text route reports 51.17% WER against 61.02% for direct synthesis on the 460 evaluated sentences; the "more fluid, natural interaction" claimed for direct synthesis (Appendix D.4) is untested. Listener WERs of 62.55% (healthy, vocalized) and 50.82% (one ALS participant, silent) stay far above 11.89% to 12.2% for silent EMG on the Gaddy benchmark [@lee2026gets; @benster2024crossmodal], with other corpora and scoring.
